questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country where you can still get the Erasmus Grant

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A whole welcome week was planned for new students and exchange students. Guided tours around campus, how to use the library etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance from other students studying in the same field and exchange coordinators

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard to find off campus. When you are only there for 4 months its hard to find someone who is interested. I did contact people on the website Spareroom and Facebook, and from there I found a place

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is way easier to stay on campus and use the accommodations that the University provides. I ended up staying with a family, which was a nice experience being a part of a family from the place. You will always something in the end, and it is easier when you are there. My advice is, if future exchange students wants to live off campus, they should arrive earlier, stay in a hostel - it is way easier to find a place to stay when you are in the country.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was very clear and easy understandable. You book a time through a mail they did send, then you arrive and they help you and it was very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Other students, people helping showing the way and the exchange coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful but it was hard to figure out which courses I could take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very easy, just talk to other students or go to campus and ask for help and they will tell you what to do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was higher than what I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Really good teachers and professors, ready to help and answer questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Structure and Function of Proteins 
Immunology 
Molecular Genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Immunology, a very good and interesting course 
Structure and Function of Proteins, small tests every week to make you keep following up and no final exam

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing unexpected, I was planning on spending a lot of money on tours around the country and to other countries around

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is less expensive than back home, and the same by going out for food. Rent and housing is more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! Almost too many societies you can be a part of including sport, cultural and other social things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Societies. From Scandinavia, the Scandi Society. If you are knitting, another society for that. If you like sport or Taylor Swift, there are societies for that

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on the trip with the Erasmus Programs, they have tours all over the country. Go out, see museums, hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Scottish people are so nice and very helpful to let you know about the best spots in town.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Become a part of all the whatsapp groups! Its a good way to meet people and see what events others are attending.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only that you cant buy alcohol after 10pm and going out everything closes at 3am or 1am. Otherwise it was very similar

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People being so welcoming, the nature and the city it self - it was like being a main character in a movie.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Become a part of the WhatsApp groups
Use all the free opportunities for students through all the societies 
Join societies and use the library to study

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take some interesting courses, use all the student discounts and societies to meet friends from all over the world

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of amazing people from all over the world, friends for life. Having some interesting courses - now I know what master I will take back home in Copenhagen

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning in a new way. At this point I have gotten used to the lectures and how everything works in Copenhagen - in Edinburgh things were different but very good as well - but getting used to the differences was a challenge

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
